ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: At the bottom of the image is a benzene ring, and two adjacent positions on the benzene ring are respectively connected to an aldehyde group bearing hydrogen (-C(=O)H, which can be written as -CHO) and an amino group (-NH2). The image also depicts an upper fragment containing R, R1, O− and multiple curved arrows. Reasoning: According to the problem statement and method draft, it is necessary to ignore the curved arrows and focus on the stable structural skeleton; on the lower benzene ring, -NH2 and -CHO are in an ortho relationship, so this structure is o-aminobenzaldehyde. Writing it as SMILES, one can start from the aromatic carbon connected to the amino group as Nc1ccccc1, and attach the aldehyde group C=O to the adjacent aromatic carbon, obtaining Nc1ccccc1C=O.

raw_record.question_text: What is the SMILES expression of the transition-state structure shown in the image, ignoring the arrows?

method.method_draft: First inspect the image and discard the curved arrows. Focus on the drawn stable structural skeleton: a benzene ring with -NH2 and -CHO on adjacent carbons. Translate this ortho-aminobenzaldehyde connectivity into SMILES by starting at the amino substituent attached to an aromatic ring, traversing the six-membered aromatic ring, and attaching the aldehyde at the adjacent ring carbon, yielding Nc1ccccc1C=O.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中下方是一个苯环，苯环上相邻的两个位置分别连有一个带氢的醛基（-C(=O)H，可写作 -CHO）和一个氨基（-NH2）。图中还画有上方含 R、R1、O− 的片段以及多条弯箭头。推理：按题意和方法草案，需要忽略弯箭头，并聚焦稳定结构骨架；下方苯环上 -NH2 与 -CHO 为邻位关系，因此该结构是邻氨基苯甲醛。将其写成 SMILES，可从氨基连接的芳香碳开始书写为 Nc1ccccc1，并在相邻芳香碳接醛基 C=O，得到 Nc1ccccc1C=O。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct visual-to-SMILES route: identify the relevant displayed molecule and encode its substituents and ring connectivity, rather than using reaction-arrow interpretation.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the chemical drawing while ignoring all curved arrows and charge/motion annotations. Identify the lower aromatic structure as a benzene ring bearing two adjacent substituents: an amino group, -NH2, and a formyl/aldehyde group, -C(=O)H.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the prompt instruction that the requested output is a SMILES expression and that arrows in the transition-state drawing should be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: aromatic benzene atoms are written with lowercase c; an amino substituent attached to an aromatic carbon can be written as N attached to c; an aldehyde substituent is written as C=O with the implicit H on the carbonyl carbon; adjacent/ortho substitution on benzene can be encoded by placing the two substituents on neighboring ring positions.
